first.rationale: Both onboarding completion and activation are down 4-6% QoQ. memory_31 and memory_86 provide the most direct evidence that simplified onboarding drives measurable improvements in both completion rates and early adoption. Verifying these two will confirm the effect sizes and implementation details before committing resources. While promotional_pricing addresses the competitive threat, the current activation and onboarding drops suggest product funnel friction is the primary lever we can control this week. Simplifying onboarding targets the root symptom (completion down 4%), should improve activation as a byproduct, and carries lower downside risk than pricing changes. Enterprise_sales_assist and referral_incentive address different segments and do not directly address the onboarding completion regression. A standard_experiment allows measurement of impact on both completion and downstream activation without broad exposure before validation.

final.rationale: Verified archive records confirm that simplified onboarding drives +13% completion lift and +3% retention improvement (exp_86), with +9% activation and +4% qualified revenue on SMB specifically (exp_31). Current onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ—both direct indicators of funnel friction. The verified precedent shows this intervention addresses the root symptom, improves downstream engagement, and strengthens retention rather than degrading it. While competitor pricing pressure is real, it is external; the onboarding regression is controllable. A standard_experiment on simplified onboarding targets SMB (price-sensitive segment most exposed to competitive threat) and should yield measurable completion and activation recovery within the week. The retention uplift from exp_86 (+3%) suggests this also supports long-term qualified revenue stability. Lower implementation complexity and faster feedback cycle than promotional pricing or enterprise restructuring.
